notes: §1985:VI.5.7.3 SR2: "Data description entries subordinate to a CD, FD, or SD entry must have level-numbers with the values 01 through, 49, 66, or 88." VisitLevelNumber classifies every level-number by the entry that contains it (Classify): a data description entry under a file description or sort-merge description entry takes the FileRecord arm and one under a communication description entry the CommunicationRecord arm, and both arms permit 1 through 49, 66 and 88 only (Permits over the table For reads), reporting COBOL1746 for any other value and for a spelling of more than two digits. The pass has no edition test, so 85 reaches it as every edition does; the CD arm, which 2023 no longer has, is kept in the same table. Probed at --std 85: level-numbers 77, 50, 55, 00, 99, 78 and 001 are refused under an FD, 77 and 55 under an SD, and 77 and 50 under a CD; 1, 2, 01, 02, 05, 49, 66 (RENAMES) and 88 compile under an FD, an SD and a CD. The witness writes 77 R2 PIC X(10) after the 01 entry of an FD and is refused with COBOL1746.

next.reason: For FD and SD the rule is kept: §2023:13.18.33.3 SR2 'Data description entries subordinate to a FD or SD entry shall have level-numbers with the values 66, 88, or 1 through 49', and §2023:13.18.33.3 SR3 lets 1 through 9 be written as 01 through 09. 1985 also covers entries subordinate to a CD. 2023 has no communication section and no rule for CD entries, so that part of the requirement is gone.
